extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of bulk gasoline terminals and pipeline breakout stations; facility environmental/compliance managers; state and federal compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and reporting requirements (monitoring, recordkeeping, definitions, and procedures for claims/exceptions) for bulk gasoline terminals and pipeline breakout stations under the NESHAP/NSPS subparts. Covers what to monitor, what to report, formats/methods for submission, and timelines for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission using CEDRI when template available
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning on July 8, 2024, or once the report template for this subpart has been available on the CEDRI website for one year (whichever is later), submit all subsequent reports using the appropriate electronic report template on the CEDRI website and follow the specified procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date templates become available will be listed on the CEDRI website. Unless an alternate schedule is approved by the Administrator/delegated authority, reports must be submitted by the subpart-specified deadline regardless of submission method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required general facility information in reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must include facility name; physical address (city, county, State); latitude and longitude in decimal degrees with at least five decimal places; contact person information (name, mailing address, telephone, email); date of report and beginning/ending dates of reporting period; and a certifying statement by a responsible official with name, title, and signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitted via CEDRI the certifier's electronic signature replaces the handwritten signature requirement and the date of report is not required to be provided separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS deviation reporting — combustion/pressure/TOC exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: For each thermal oxidation system (combustion-zone temperature monitoring), each pressure CPMS (pressure monitoring), and each vapor recovery TOC CEMS when monitoring indicates excursions (3-hour rolling average below/above or pressure exceeded), report date and start time, duration (hours), each 3-hour rolling average value (indicate whether methane is excluded for TOC), unique CMS identifier, make/model/date of last calibration, cause of deviation and corrective action taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to deviations from operating limits specified in applicable sections (§60.502a, §60.504a, etc.). Provide the full set of 3-hour rolling averages observed during the deviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS outage/inoperable reporting and limited-alternative reporting for TOC CEMS
rubrics_metrics.description: When a CPMS or TOC CEMS was not operating or was out of control during gasoline cargo tank loading (or vapor recovery operating), report date and start time, duration (hours), unique CMS identifier, make/model/date of last calibration, and cause and corrective action. For TOC CEMS outages using the limited alternative under §60.504a(e), indicate use of the limited alternative and either state that no deviations occurred while using it or report the counts of specified deviation types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the limited alternative is used, report counts (enter 0 if none) for: (1) adsorption cycles where quantity loaded exceeded the operating limit; (2) desorption cycles where vacuum pressure was below the specified average; (3) desorption cycles where purge gas quantity was below the specified average; (4) desorption cycles where vacuum/purge duration was less than the specified average. Also include corrective actions and cause of outage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare monitoring deviations — pilot flame and visible emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For each flare or thermal oxidation system using the flare monitoring alternative, report date and start/end times for: (A) each 15-minute block with at least one minute when gasoline vapors were routed to the flare and no pilot flame was present; (B) each 2-hour period during which visible emissions exceeded a total of 5 minutes (report number of minutes observed or an estimate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When visible emissions exceed the threshold, provide minutes observed during the observation or best-estimate cumulative minutes for the 2-hour period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare operating-limits reporting (15-minute periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each 15-minute period when applicable operating limits in §63.670(d)-(f) were not met, identify the specific operating limit not met and provide the corresponding detailed information depending on monitoring method used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the sub-items below depending on selected monitoring approach (loading rate, supplemental gas flow rate, or other parameter monitoring):

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare reporting for loading-rate monitoring alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: If using loading-rate operating limits (alone or combined with supplemental gas flow rate monitoring), report the required minimum ratio and the actual ratio of gasoline loaded to total product loaded for the rolling 15-minute period, and if applicable, the required minimum quantity and actual quantity of gasoline loaded (gallons) for the rolling 15-minute period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data for the rolling 15-minute period during which the operating limit was not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare reporting for supplemental gas flow-rate monitoring alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: If using the supplemental gas flow rate monitoring alternative, report the required minimum supplemental gas flow rate and the actual supplemental gas flow rate (include units) for the 15-minute block during which the operating limit was not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include units of flow (e.g., scfm) and the 15-minute block values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare reporting for other parameter-monitoring systems
rubrics_metrics.description: If using parameter monitoring systems other than the loading-rate or supplemental gas flow-rate options, report the value of the net heating value operating parameter(s) during the deviation, determined following the methods in §63.670(k) through (n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §63.670(k)-(n) methods to compute and report net heating value parameters for the deviation period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting when vapors routed but monitoring not performed
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the start date, start time, and duration in minutes for each period when vapors displaced from gasoline cargo tanks during product loading were routed to the flare or thermal oxidation system and the applicable monitoring was not performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include precise start times and duration in minutes for each such period.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS-specific information for flare/thermal-oxidizer incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: For each instance involving CMS reported under flare provisions, provide a unique CMS identifier, the make/model/date of last calibration check, the cause of deviation or downtime, and corrective action taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors CMS reporting for other systems—include the same identifying and corrective-action details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor-tightness documentation missing — cargo tank reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For any instance where liquid product was loaded into a cargo tank without required vapor-tightness documentation, report cargo tank owner and address, cargo tank identification number, date/time of loading without documentation, and date proper documentation was received or statement that it was never received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide owner contact/address and explicit statement if documentation was never received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-submerged filling/incompatible/not-connected cargo tank reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For each instance when liquid product was loaded into a cargo tank that was not submerged-filling, lacked vapor collection compatibility, or was not properly connected, report the date/time, type of deviation (e.g., not submerged filling, incompatible equipment, not properly connected), and cargo tank identification number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about the deviation type to allow determination of applicable corrective requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak detection and repair (LDAR) program implementation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must implement an LDAR program for all equipment in gasoline service and minimize gasoline vapor losses according to the section's requirements, performing monthly inspections (paragraph (b) or (c) as applicable) and complying with repair timing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly inspections may use sight, sound, and smell detection methods. Each piece of equipment must be inspected during loading of a gasoline cargo tank. Maintain logs and follow repair/repair-delay provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly leak inspection procedures and logbook requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform monthly inspections of all equipment in gasoline service, record detections in a logbook signed by the owner/operator at completion of each inspection. The log must include a list/summary/diagram of all equipment in gasoline service at the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections occur during cargo tank loading. The logbook signature certifies completion of each inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak repair timing and delay-of-repair provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a leak is detected, an initial repair attempt must be made as soon as practicable but no later than 5 calendar days after detection; repair or replacement must be completed within 15 calendar days after detection, except where delay of repair is allowed upon demonstration to the Administrator that repair within 15 days is not feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If delay is requested, demonstration to the Administrator must justify infeasibility of 15-day repair and follow specified procedures for delay of repair reporting and tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak inspection reporting elements (leaks detected during required inspections)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each leak detected during required leak inspections, report date of inspection; leak determination method (OGI or Method 21); total number and type of equipment for which leaks were detected; totals for equipment repaired within 15 days; totals for equipment with no repair attempt within 5 calendar days; and totals for equipment placed on delay of repair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break out totals by equipment type and provide counts for each reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting for leaks identified under §63.502a(j)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For leaks identified under this provision, report total number and type of equipment for which leaks were identified; totals repaired within 15 calendar days; totals with no repair attempt within 5 calendar days; and totals placed on delay of repair as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the same breakout and counts as required for scheduled inspections, focused on §63.502a(j)(2) identified leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay-of-repair list tracking and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the total number of leaks on the delay-of-repair list at the start and end of the reporting period. For each leak that was on the delay list at any time during the reporting period, report unique equipment ID, type of equipment, leak determination method (OGI, Method 21, or audio/visual/olfactory), reasons repair was not feasible within 15 days, and if applicable, the date repair was completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit equipment identifiers and narrative reasons for infeasibility; include completion dates where repairs were later made.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-deviations statement when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: If there were no deviations from emission limitations, operating parameters, or work practice standards during the reporting period, provide a statement to that effect. Similarly, if there were no CMS inoperable or out-of-control periods, provide a statement that none occurred during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise affirmative statement suffices where there were no deviations or CMS outages during the reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for first and subsequent semiannual reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The first semiannual report covers from the date the source first becomes an affected facility through the last day of the month five months later and must be submitted on or before the last day of the month two months after the last date covered. Subsequent semiannual reports cover 6-calendar-month periods and are due on or before the last day of the month two months after the period end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: facility becomes affected on April 15; first semiannual report covers April 15–Sept 30 and is due Nov 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission process and public availability; CBI handling rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports submitted via CEDRI/CDX will be made publicly available. Do not use CEDRI to submit information claimed as Confidential Business Information (CBI). To assert a CBI claim, submit a complete file in the specified format to the EPA CBI office including the CBI-marked portions, and also submit the same file with CBI omitted to CDX. All CBI claims must be asserted at submission time; items submitted via CEDRI cannot later be claimed as CBI. Emissions data are not entitled to CBI protection and will be made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information not marked as CBI may be authorized for public release without prior notice. CBI is handled per 40 CFR part 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred CBI submission methods and postal backup
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred method to submit CBI is electronically (email attachments, FTP, or other file sharing) to oaqpscbi@epa.gov; flag ERT files to Measurement Policy Group leader and other files to Gasoline Distribution Sector Lead. If electronic transfer is not possible, mail CBI to the specified EPA postal address; mailed materials should be double wrapped and clearly marked so markings do not show through the outer envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If files exceed email size limits and you lack a file-sharing service, email oaqpscbi@epa.gov to request a file transfer link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of EPA system outage — eligibility and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: To assert an EPA system outage for failure to timely submit electronically, you must: (1) be precluded from accessing CEDRI/CDX due to outage; (2) the outage must have occurred within the period beginning five business days prior to the submission due date; (3) outage may be planned/unplanned; (4) notify the Administrator in writing as soon as possible after you knew (or should have known) the outage could cause a delay; and (5) provide a written description including dates/times CDX/CEDRI was accessed and unavailable, rationale attributing delay to outage, measures taken/to minimize delay, and proposed reporting date (or date you already reported). The Administrator has discretion to accept the claim. The report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after outage resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep detailed access logs to support outage claims (dates/times) and explain mitigation steps and proposed new submission date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of force majeure — eligibility, definition, and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: To assert a force majeure for failure to timely submit electronically, the event must occur or have lingering effects within the period beginning five business days prior to the due date. Force majeure is an event beyond the control of the affected facility (examples: hurricanes, earthquakes, floods, acts of war/terrorism, large-scale power outages, equipment failure or safety hazard beyond facility control). Notify the Administrator in writing as soon as possible and provide a written description of the event, rationale attributing the delay to the event, measures taken/to minimize the delay, and the proposed reporting date (or actual report date). Acceptance and any extension are at the Administrator's discretion; reporting must occur as soon as possible after the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the event, impacts, and mitigation; supply proposed timelines and evidence supporting that the event prevented timely submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: General duty to operate and maintain consistent with good practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must operate and maintain affected sources, including air pollution control and monitoring equipment, in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices for minimizing emissions at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of compliance with operation and maintenance requirements may be based on monitoring results, review of O&M procedures and records, and inspection of the source. The general duty does not require further efforts to reduce emissions once the applicable standard levels have been achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of key terms used in the subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: The subpart defines terms that determine applicability and compliance, including: 'Bulk gasoline terminal' (thresholds before and after May 8, 2027; throughput definitions), 'Flare' (thermal combustion device with open or shrouded flame not emitting through a conveyance suitable for performance test), 'Gasoline' (petroleum distillate or blend with Reid vapor pressure ≥ 4.0 psi), 'Pipeline breakout station' (facility along pipeline with storage vessels used to relieve surges/receive/store gasoline), 'Submerged filling' (fill pipe discharge no more than 6 inches from tank bottom), and 'Thermal oxidation system' (enclosed combustion device that emits pollutants through a conveyance suitable for performance test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions supersede definitions in other parts as specified; throughput metrics are facility-design-based and may be limited by enforceable conditions discoverable by the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards — Loading racks compliance options and emission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of loading racks must meet either §60.502 (with specified exceptions) or §60.502a (with specified exceptions) as applicable. Emissions from vapor collection and processing systems due to loading must not exceed 10 mg total organic compounds per liter of gasoline loaded, or comply with §60.502a(c) requirements for all loading racks. Discontinue loading any cargo tank failing vapor tightness until repair/certification per §63.425 is documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms 'affected facility' and 'vapor-tight gasoline cargo tanks' are defined for subpart purposes. Compliance dates vary based on facility construction/startup dates (see detailed subparagraphs for dates). As an alternative to certain pressure-monitoring provisions, owners/operators may design/operate systems to prevent gauge pressure exceeding test limits and ensure pressure-vacuum vents do not open below test limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards — Storage vessels equipment and vapor concentration control
rubrics_metrics.description: Gasoline storage vessels with design capacity ≥75 m3 must be equipped per §60.112b(a)(1)-(4) (with certain exceptions) or meet alternative subpart WW requirements. Internal floating control systems must maintain vapor concentration above the floating roof at or below 25% of the LEL on a 5-minute rolling average without purge gas; deviations are inspection failures requiring remedy and re-monitoring. Fitting controls for external floating roofs must be installed by the next complete emptying/degassing or by May 8, 2034, whichever first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance timeframes depend on construction/startup date categories; use §63.425(j) methods to determine compliance with the 25% LEL requirement; remedial timeframes follow §60.113b(a)(2) or §63.1063(e) as applicable.
